diagnosis.question: Why do the post-video review-ask surfaces (everything except the in_app thankyou screen) generate essentially zero reviews, and where is the untapped review moment?
hypotheses_considered: H1: The delivery email simply has no review ask (structural absence), so there is nothing to convert.
H2: The review ask exists on preview/share but is buried below the share CTA (prominence).
H3: The people on preview/share are gift receivers who cannot leave a verified-purchase review (audience/structural).
H4: The review moment is mistimed — the working ask (in_app thankyou) fires before the user has seen the finished video (anticipation, not payoff).
diagnosis.evidence_gathered: Read the actual code paths: resolve-video.js sendVideoEmail() is the LIVE delivery email (called after completion in the email-first flow) and contains NO review link (confirms H1). api/send-video-email.js has a review ask but is dead (no client caller) and broken (hardcoded ASIN B0DK1RF3TZ matching no in-app product; raw Amazon link, untracked). video-preview.html already renders the review ask as a prominent orange card that pulses/scrolls after share (June's work) yet produces ~0 clicks — so H2 'just make it prominent' is already spent. Funnel-report both windows: 10/10 (this) and 4/9 (prior) review clicks come from in_app thankyou; preview/share ~0. Session replay (204 claim sessions this window, 215 prior) was used to characterise the separate claim-gate leak (67% vs 69% never type; 79% of never-typers dwell >5s).
diagnosis.what_the_evidence_supports: H1 + H4. The single highest-reach, highest-intent review surface we own — the delivery email everyone opens to watch their video — asks for nothing, and the ask that DOES work fires one step too early (before the payoff). Putting a tracked, correctly-targeted, honest-review ask into that email addresses both.
diagnosis.what_it_cannot_distinguish: I cannot measure how many reviews the delivery email would produce, because it currently has no (tracked) link — there is no baseline. I also cannot verify from data whether the person opening the delivery email is predominantly the buyer (verified-review-eligible) or the receiver; the in-app role split is receiver-heavy, which could cap the ceiling (H3 unresolved). And PostHog's person-linked funnels are 403, so the claim-gate leak has no frozen before/after this cycle.

plan.title: Add a tracked, honest-review ask at the payoff moment: put a correctly-targeted 'Leave an honest review' link in the LIVE video-delivery email
plan.targets: Post-video review capture — the video-delivery email surface (currently zero review asks), feeding the objective (reviews) directly.
plan.mechanism: The delivery email (resolve-video.js sendVideoEmail) is opened by every finisher to watch their finished video — the emotional payoff. Today it has one CTA ('Watch & Share') and no review ask. Add a SECONDARY, visually subordinate review section below the primary CTA whose link points at /api/review-redirect?email=<session.email>&sku=<session.sku>&source=video_email. review-redirect already logs the click (Supabase phase=email_redirect, PostHog, Klaviyo) and 302s to the correct Amazon create-review page. It will be extended minimally to (a) accept sku and resolve sku->asin via the existing master_products lookup (falling back to its current default ASIN B0DVR6VBRR if unresolved), and (b) accept an optional source param (defaulting to the existing 'email' so Email 5/6 links are byte-for-byte unchanged) so delivery-email clicks are separately measurable under a new SOURCES.VIDEO_EMAIL. resolve-video.js's session select adds `sku`.
plan.assumed_cause: H1 (the payoff-moment surface asks for nothing) combined with H4 (the working ask fires pre-payoff). The bet is that a warm ask placed where delight actually lands will capture reviews that currently go uncaptured, without competing with anything.
plan.why_the_rate_is_what_it_is: Review clicks are near-entirely produced by the one prominent ask on the in_app thankyou screen; every other surface either has no ask (delivery email) or an already-prominent-but-ignored one (preview/share). Reviewers give ~30 seconds of effort in a moment of goodwill right after experiencing something delightful; the delivery email is that moment and currently offers no path to act on the goodwill.
what_would_have_to_be_true: A meaningful share of delivery-email openers are buyers able to leave a verified-purchase review (not only gift receivers).
sku is present on the video_sessions row at send time so the correct ASIN can be resolved (fallback to default ASIN otherwise).
A secondary review link does not pull enough people away from 'Watch & Share' to reduce sharing/recipient reach.
Adding 'honest review' framing (Amazon TOS) does not read as cold — copy stays warm and human, and the discount is never linked to reviewing.
plan.second_order_effects: The email's primary purpose is to get the creator to watch and SHARE (share -> recipient opens video.html -> reach). A review link could divert a few from sharing, so it stays visually secondary and below the 'Watch & Share' button, which remains the sole primary CTA. Downstream, routing through review-redirect means these clicks now also mark the Klaviyo profile review_clicked=true and land in Supabase as phase=email_redirect/source=video_email — making the surface measurable for future cycles (today it is invisible). One further step out: because review-redirect resolves the correct per-product ASIN, reviews land on the product the person actually bought, so they are verified-eligible and count — the dead file's single wrong ASIN would have sent everyone to the wrong listing.
plan.strongest_case_against: A sceptic would say: the delivery-email audience is receiver-heavy (in-app role split is receiver-dominated), receivers can't leave verified-purchase reviews, so a payoff-moment ask converts near zero and you've added clutter to a working share email — risking shares to gain nothing. My answer: (1) the ask is secondary and below the unchanged primary CTA, so share risk is minimal and watchable via share_completed; (2) even the prior window shows non-thankyou surfaces CAN produce review clicks (preview_receiver 3, email_redirect 2), so the ceiling is not zero; (3) the change also fixes a genuine correctness/measurement gap (untracked, wrong-ASIN review links) regardless of conversion; (4) it is explicitly labelled measurable:false — I will not claim it worked without a SIGNIFICANT result, so the downside is bounded and the upside compounds.
plan.expected_effect: A few additional honest review clicks per fortnight at the payoff moment, correctly attributed to the product bought, with the surface becoming measurable from next cycle. Not expected to clear the significance floor.

tradeoff.gained: A tracked, correctly-targeted honest-review ask on the highest-reach post-video surface we control (opened by ~36 finishers/fortnight), plus fixing an untracked/wrong-ASIN review link — directly serving the objective (reviews).
tradeoff.risked: Preview/share behaviour could dip slightly if the secondary link distracts from 'Watch & Share'; baseline to watch is share_completed = 9 this window (9 prior) and share_page_opened = 21 (19 prior). Review clicks currently arriving via the Klaviyo reminder emails (phase=email_redirect, source=email) are 0 this window and 2 prior; this change adds a separately-sourced (source=video_email) touchpoint and does NOT modify Email 5/6, so that channel is unaffected.
unverified_assumptions: Whether delivery-email openers are predominantly buyers (verified-review-eligible) or receivers — cannot be determined from current data.

Whether B0DK1RF3TZ in the dead send-video-email.js was ever intentional (e.g. a flagship/brand ASIN) — owner should confirm the canonical review ASIN/logic; I align to the maintained in-app per-SKU resolution.
Whether ROS master_products env keys are configured in the deploy so sku->asin resolves (graceful fallback to default ASIN if not).

plan.differs_from_past_attempt: Not PR #8 (claim-page layout — untouched here). Not the owner-rejected discount-before-email or printed-number moves (no claim-page or discount change). Not the June preview/share prominence rework (different surface entirely — the delivery email; and I am not re-running 'make the existing ask more prominent', I am adding an ask where none exists). Not the Klaviyo Email 5/6 reminders (out of scope, untouched) — this is the repo-owned Resend delivery email.

Hit /api/review-redirect?email=<test>&sku=PTT-GREEN1&source=video_email and confirm it (a) 302s to the correct per-ASIN Amazon create-review URL, (b) inserts a Supabase row phase=email_redirect source=video_email, then delete that test row by id. Backward-compat: /api/review-redirect?email=<test>&asin=... (no source) still logs source=email (Email 5/6 unaffected). Then re-measure ~2026-08-11: funnel-report review clicks by source, isolating source=video_email; significance-test only if counts ever allow.

Re-prominence the preview/share review card — rejected: June already ran that mechanism and it is ~0.

Attack the claim gate with a copy/hero change ('You Won a Prize!' -> box-voice) — rejected: claim-page presentation is spent ground (PR #8) and this cycle's mandate is mechanics-or-leave-it there.
